summary:
Public Law 119-48 (formerly H.J. Res. 104) is a joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code (the Congressional Review Act), of a rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM). The resolution's primary operative mechanism is the statutory nullification of the specified BLM rule.

Specifically, the joint resolution disapproves the BLM rule relating to the "Miles City Field Office Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan Amendment," which was issued on November 20, 2024. The resolution expressly provides that this rule "shall have no force or effect," thereby repealing the rule's legal validity and rendering it a nullity.

The resolution incorporates a condition precedent to this disapproval by referencing a letter of opinion from the Government Accountability Office (GAO), dated June 25, 2025. This opinion, printed in the Congressional Record on June 26, 2025 (pages S3552-S3554), concluded that the BLM record of decision and resource management plan amendment constitutes a "rule" under the Congressional Review Act, thereby subjecting it to the congressional disapproval procedures authorized by chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code. 

The joint resolution was approved on December 11, 2025. Legislative history indicates it was considered and passed by the House of Representatives on September 3, 2025, and considered and passed by the Senate on October 7 and 8, 2025. The resolution contains no separate authorizations of appropriations or new budget authority.
